archetype.name: Pocket Passer (in survival mode)
archetype.definition: A big-armed, rhythm-based pocket thrower whose game was built on volume and arm talent, now playing behind a collapsing protection unit and leaning on his legs and short throws to limit damage.

report.headline: Sacks and late-game turnovers have buried a passer whose clean dropbacks look ordinary
report.take:
Herbert's career is six years of steady, top-third production: EPA per play ranked between 10th and 25th every season, with passing-yard ranks as high as 2nd. This year he sits 43rd of 55 in EPA per dropback at -0.166, by far the worst of his career. The setting matters. The Chargers rank 32nd in offensive EPA and 32nd in pass rate over expected at -10.3, so Harbaugh is running more than anyone in neutral situations. Herbert is throwing only 27.4 times a game.

The odd part is that his completed-pass profile is almost exactly league average. His 6.76 yards per attempt matches the league's 6.76, and his 62.4% completion rate sits right on the 62.2% norm. The collapse lives in the negative plays. He has taken 39 sacks at a 12.5% rate (50th of 55), and he has been hit or sacked on 22.1% of dropbacks. He also has 11 interceptions and 8 turnover-worthy fumbles. It is concentrated where it hurts most: -0.285 EPA per play in one-score games, and -0.834 in close fourth quarters, where 10 of 33 plays ended in sacks.

The last three games show a deliberate change of shape. Attempts are down to 20.7 a game, and intended air yards fell to 5.6 and 5.2 in Weeks 10 and 11. He is holding the ball longer (3.46 and 3.03 seconds) and running more. The interceptions nearly stopped (1.6% rate), and EPA per dropback climbed to -0.046. The cost is a 20.5% sack rate: he is trading picks for sacks. His 16.4 fantasy points a game over that stretch rest on two rushing touchdowns, which is fragile scoring. One more note on accuracy: his bad-throw rate is ninth-lowest of 45, so the -4.8-point CPOE drop from last year reflects where and under what duress the ball is going more than wild misses.

All of this is on hold behind a concussion. He is questionable after entering protocol following the Jets loss. If he clears, the Patriots' pass defense is the softest he has seen in weeks. Their one real strength, getting home with the rush, aims straight at his biggest problem.

strengths.title: Legs as the pressure valve
strengths.body: He ranks 3rd among qualifying QBs in rushing yards, and scrambles have been mildly positive at +0.087 EPA each. That is one of the few things in this offense that works when the pocket breaks down. This isn't new: he ran for 498 yards last season (2nd), so the mobility is a durable part of his game and a floor for fantasy value. A concussion could make the staff more cautious about designed runs, though.

strengths.title: Recent turnover clean-up
strengths.body: Over Weeks 9-11 his interception rate fell to 1.6% and his EPA per dropback rose to -0.046, near league average. He got there by throwing shorter and taking fewer chances. It is a sustainable way to limit damage in a run-first offense, but it caps his ceiling and shifts the cost onto sacks.

strengths.title: Wideouts, especially to the left
strengths.body: Throws to the left have produced +0.147 EPA per attempt, and his three receivers all carry positive EPA per target. McConkey leads at +0.379. The passing game works when the ball goes to wideouts. Deep throws are even slightly positive despite a 36.7% completion rate, so the arm still produces chunk plays when he has time.

concerns.title: Sacks are the whole story
concerns.body: A 12.5% sack rate and a 39.3% pressure-to-sack rate are near the bottom of the league, and the last three weeks pushed the rate to 20.5%. The line shares blame, since the offense ranks 31st in hit rate allowed. But his career pressure-to-sack rate has climbed from 17.1% as a rookie to 33.3% in 2024, so holding the ball to avoid mistakes is a growing trait, not a one-year fluke.

concerns.title: Interceptions beyond ten yards
concerns.body: Nine of his 11 picks have come on throws of 10+ air yards. On those throws he completes 46.7% with a -5.5 CPOE, and the intermediate range is worse at -7.1. Interceptions are a career pattern (15 in 2021, 13 last year, ranked 60th of 63). His recent retreat to short throws treats the symptom rather than fixing it.

concerns.title: Close games and tight ends
concerns.body: In one-score games he is at -0.285 EPA per play, and close fourth quarters have been disastrous at -0.834. The structure leaves him little room: a run-heavy offense means late obvious passing downs against teed-off rushes. His two tight ends both bleed EPA, Kolar at -0.371 per target, which shrinks the reliable short options when he needs them.

trend.note: Per-game passing EPA bottomed out at -11.5 and -11.8 in Weeks 6 and 8. It has improved each week since, to -4.6, -1.6 and +2.6. Volume and sacks moved the wrong way during that climb, so the improvement is in efficiency, not output.

nextGame.headline: Soft Patriots secondary, but their pass rush hits his weakness
nextGame.body:
New England's pass defense ranks 25th in EPA. It allows the 29th-worst explosive pass rate and ranks 27th on deep throws and 26th on short ones. Opposing WR1s and WR2s have been the most efficient in the league against it (0.83 and 0.61 EPA a target, 32nd and 31st). That lines up with where Herbert's passing actually works: his wideouts. The catch is the rush. The Patriots rank 8th in sack rate and 10th in hit rate, which is exactly the matchup for a quarterback taking sacks on 12.5% of dropbacks. Tight ends get nothing here (TE1 EPA allowed ranks 3rd), so the ball should go outside. The game is indoors.

Availability drives everything. Herbert is questionable in concussion protocol, and if he doesn't clear, none of this applies. On the other side, starting corner Carlton Davis III is out, which weakens an already soft coverage group. The Patriots' offense is without Drake Maye (fractured fibula), and A.J. Brown is doubtful. That explains the 35.5 total and LAC -1.5, and points to a low-scoring, one-score game. That is his worst game state this year, so a better defensive opponent doesn't guarantee a clean day.

keyMatchups.title: Chargers wideouts vs. depleted secondary
keyMatchups.body: The Patriots have been worst in the league in EPA allowed to WR1s, and their starting corner is out. Herbert's receivers are his only consistently positive targets. With Davis sidelined, this is the clearest path to chunk gains.

keyMatchups.title: Patriots pass rush vs. his sacks
keyMatchups.body: New England's 8th-ranked sack rate meets a quarterback with a 20.5% sack rate over his last three games. If he keeps holding the ball to avoid interceptions, drives will die on sacks even against a soft secondary.

keyMatchups.title: Low total, tight game script
keyMatchups.body: With Maye out, the Book's 35.5 total implies a grinding one-score game. Herbert has been at his worst in that state, and his team passes less than anyone, so passing volume should stay low.

nextGame.watch: Whether he clears protocol. If he does, watch whether the quick, short-throw approach of the last three weeks holds against a rush that can finish.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the post-Week-8 version: low volume, short throws, real rushing value, and efficiency near league average on clean dropbacks. The structure, a run-first offense at the bottom of the league in pass rate over expected, is not changing. Passing yardage should stay in the 150-200 range, with touchdowns well under one and a half a game. The interception rate should land between his recent clean stretch and his early-season mess. Throws beyond ten yards are where his picks come from, and he can't avoid them entirely in obvious passing downs.

Two things will regress. A rushing touchdown in each of the last two games is not a rate to bank on, and the 16.4 fantasy points a game over the last three will drift down with it. Sacks will remain the defining cost. They have been trending worse for years and the line isn't protecting him. The concussion adds uncertainty to both his availability and how freely he runs.
swingFactors: Concussion recovery and how freely he runs afterward
Whether the protection improves enough to cut the sack rate
Game scripts that force him out of the short-throw shell

confidence.note: Ten full starts, but a recent style shift, rushing TDs on small volume and an active concussion cloud the outlook.
